subject: parallel numba kernels run FASTER under host load
observation: C1b: d64 r64 B4096, numba_par x1.26 and nb_bucket_c3 x1.15 wall throughput at burn8 vs idle; single-thread numba_1 x0.84.
expected: C1 and B's bounty caveat both predicted parallel kernels lose throughput under load.
surprise: sign of the load effect reversed for parallel kernels only
discriminator: same cells with CPU affinity pinned and power plan fixed; count thread migrations and core frequency under idle vs sham vs burn

subject: closed-loop brains lose at 8 train seeds, catch or lead open loop at 128
observation: E6: held-out 2.0 vs 45.9 (w1), 53.4 vs 90.3 (w3), 57.1 vs 87.3 (w4) at 8 train seeds. E8: at 128 seeds closed 95.9 vs open 93.5 (w4), 63.9 vs 58.6 (w1), tie w3.
expected: E5/E6 read: closed loop overfits and loses.
surprise: direction reverses with train-seed count; the mechanism (seed diversity vs search budget vs genome size) is not localized
discriminator: hold genomes fixed and vary train seeds only; then hold seeds fixed and vary budget; score both on the 64 held-out seeds

subject: fewest-byte brain generalises best
observation: E9 (8 run seeds): held-out medians linear 35.5/103.2/89.9 > tt_feat 17.1/91.6/79.2 > tt_digits 8.7/78.9/62.0 in w1/w3/w4; genome bytes linear 208-344, tt_feat 3004-5316, tt_digits 11644-20868.
expected: richer TT brains should fit the worlds at least as well
surprise: ranking is inverse to genome size in all three worlds
discriminator: equalize parameter count across families (pad linear, shrink TT rank) and re-rank; or grow linear toward TT size

subject: tt_digits held-out score swings with the run RNG
observation: E7 caveat: re-running E6's TT with a new RNG moved w3 held-out 53.4 -> 87.7; E7b tt_digits w3 runs spanned 17.5..86.8 while linear stayed 84-106.
surprise: one family is several times noisier than the others under identical budgets
discriminator: fix the archive and vary only initialization; then fix initialization and vary only mutation stream

subject: end-state exactness check goes blind at full scale
observation: E1: a racy client-side archive showed 32 mismatched cells at 20 gens x 256 but 0 at 300 x 1024 (4 workers); a saturated 1089-cell grid heals lost elites.
expected: a race that loses elites is visible at any scale
surprise: the instrument's sensitivity falls to zero as the search converges
discriminator: sweep generations x batch and record the scale where detection vanishes; compare with an event-level audit of every insert

subject: a 45-byte program learns from 128 samples where tensors need 2048+
observation: C3b: from <=512 noisy samples only the in-vocabulary program learns (24/24 cells); TT/CP forms first learn at N=2048-8192.
expected: low-rank tensors are sample-efficient on low-rank targets
surprise: a symbolic program beats every tensor form by >= 4x in samples on its own vocabulary
discriminator: program targets just outside the vocabulary (one extra operator); tensor targets inside a program's vocabulary

subject: metered code learner stalls in silence or 2-4 symbol codes
observation: D1: with decoder rent beta=0.01 a (1+32) hill climber stops at gaps up to 0.69 from the exact analytic optimum; 2000 -> 8000 gens no change. D1b: 8/21 valley elites DO have an improving single move; post hoc a 1-encoder+1-decoder move fixes (0,0) 3/3 (unscored).
expected: a climber with enough generations reaches the analytic optimum
surprise: improving single moves exist but are not taken; three candidate traps (operator bundling, width valley, rent valley)
discriminator: prospective run of the 1enc+1dec operator on fresh seeds and on the rent and width cells separately

subject: affine plastic learner: 238/238 switches on fit-eligible targets, 73/130 on genome-eligible
observation: C7c (fit-based eligibility) detected 238/238 regime switches; C7e (eligibility computed from the world genomes, fixed charge column) detected 73/130.
expected: the genome-derived eligible set is the cleaner set, so detection should not fall
surprise: a more principled eligibility rule roughly halved detection
discriminator: score C7e's learner on C7c's targets and C7c's learner protocol on C7e's targets (swap one factor at a time)

subject: fitness-shuffled cheat beat the branch-point null in one rep
observation: E2b: FAKEFIT (real descent, fitness shuffled) exceeded the max of 20 null worlds in 1 of 3 reps (6.5% vs 4.7%).
expected: a cheat with no fitness signal never beats the null
surprise: transfer half of the branch-point definition is thin at max-of-20
discriminator: 100 null worlds and 10 reps of FAKEFIT; report the FAKEFIT exceedance rate with a CI

subject: a fitness gate passes a wrong world; only the trace hash catches it
observation: E4: skip_lin elites had 0 charge mismatches in 3/5 worlds and HIGHER fitness in 2; the wforge trace hash failed 32/32.
expected: a broken world lowers or scrambles fitness
surprise: removing lin_ops can raise fitness while matching final charge
discriminator: measure which state variables skip_lin leaves invariant under the fitness objective; test other one-semantic cheats against the same fitness gate
